h100-block-chronology.alt: Eight chronological 50-request blocks follow U,C,C,U,C,U,U,C. Upstream block medians are about 57.3 seconds and compiled medians about 43.7 seconds. A separate panel displays millisecond deviations from each role's overall median; no uncertainty bars are shown.
h100-block-chronology.caption: Each marker is the median of the 50 actual requests in its original chronological process block. The fixed role sequence is U,C,C,U,C,U,U,C, with U = upstream eager and C = compiled denoiser. The top panel uses a zero-based latency axis; the bottom panel shows each block median minus its own role's overall 200-request median, in milliseconds. The lower panel is a descriptive change of origin, not a speedup, noise bound or confidence interval. Block index denotes launch order, not elapsed wall-clock time. Four repeats of the same 50 scenes per role do not establish stationarity or cross-hardware generalization. Historical October 30, 2026 cohort: one NVIDIA H100 80 GB GPU and one fixed runtime. Each role has 200 measured requests from the same 50 scene groups, repeated four times; the 400 requests are not 400 independent scenes. Each request generates 24 future frames at 576 × 1024 with pretrained Vista and 50 denoising steps. Request latency includes input loading/preprocessing through host-ready frames and excludes initialization, compilation, warmups and output export. These figures describe performance and allocator memory only: held-out output-quality validation was not completed, and quality preservation is not established. No hardware cohorts are pooled.

h100-latency-memory.alt: Median latency falls from 57.338 to 43.663 seconds, while peak CUDA allocated memory rises from 52.21 to 56.22 GiB. Both bar axes start at zero. This is a performance–memory tradeoff with output quality unvalidated.
h100-latency-memory.caption: Zero-based bars compare role-wise median latency and the maximum recorded CUDA allocated-memory peak across the 200 requests in each role. Allocated bytes are converted to GiB using 2^30 bytes per GiB; this is neither reserved allocator memory nor total GPU/system memory. Median latency is 23.85% lower while peak allocated memory is 7.68% higher for the compiled denoiser. No variance or error bars are inferred for memory. The separately recorded 31.34% sequential-throughput increase uses the sum of measured request latencies, not the reciprocal of the median, and is not a concurrent-serving claim.
